messages:
Priya K.: hey everyone, Priya here — starting today. quick kube question: `kubectl config get-contexts` only shows `docker-desktop`. I need read access to `staging` and write access in a personal onboarding ns for tutorials (`platform-onboard-priya`). who should I open a ticket with and what exact info do you need? :wave:

Ava (DevEx): welcome Priya! :tada: open an infra ticket and include your corp email, manager, desired namespaces and whether you need read/write. also paste `kubectl config view --minify --flatten` so infra can see your current kubeconfig.

Priya K.: pasted my flattened kubeconfig here (it's minimal):
```
apiVersion: v1
clusters: []
contexts: []
current-context: docker-desktop
kind: Config
preferences: {}
users:
- name: docker
```

I created ticket INF-921 and linked my manager @marco_l.

onboard-bot: ticket INF-921 created and assigned to eng-infra. https://tickets.redwood/INF-921

Jon (Eng-Infra): hi Priya — quick summary of our process: we map SSO groups to k8s roles. For onboarding we usually create `platform-onboard-<firstname>` and bind `edit` for the user. For staging we'll add you to `redwood-staging-read` unless you specifically need exec/create. If you need temporary elevated perms specify duration. I've got INF-921 — I'll create the namespace and RBAC now.

Jon (Eng-Infra): done. Please verify these commands:
```
kubectl config get-contexts
kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=platform-onboard-priya
kubectl auth can-i create deployments --namespace=staging
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=platform-onboard-priya
```

Priya K.: ran them — `get-contexts` now shows `redwood-staging` and `platform-onboard-priya` contexts. `auth can-i` returned yes for listing pods in my onboarding ns and no for create in staging (that's fine). I can also `kubectl run` a test pod in my namespace. thanks! :raised_hands:

Ava (DevEx): awesome — a couple of follow-ups: 1) to switch explicitly run `kubectl config use-context redwood-staging`, 2) if your kubeconfig gets merged weirdly run `kubectl config view --flatten > ~/.kube/config && chmod 600 ~/.kube/config`, 3) if you ever need staging writes request temporary elevation in a ticket and include exact expiry (we default to 48h).

Jon (Eng-Infra): security note: we create onboarding namespaces with a NetworkPolicy that denies ingress from other namespaces by default; if you need cross-namespace access open a separate request.

Priya K.: noted — thanks both for the fast help! I'll close out INF-921 after I confirm editor access for tools.
